newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sees reasonable launch costs.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sees reasonable launch costs.

text.p: Chrysler Corp does not anticipate that new model production launches in the second half of 1997 will reduce earnings as much as the 1995 launch of its current minivans did, Chief Financial Officer Gary Valade said on Thursday.

Valade told reporters in a conference call that Chrysler plans to shut down its Bramalea, Ontario, car plant for three to four weeks this summer to launch production of the next-generation LH large car.
It also will begin production of the new Dodge Durango sport utility vehicle in Newark, Del., in September, but that startup will not involve any lost production because the plant is currently idle.

"Those launches are nothing compared to the minivan launch," Valade said. "We will lose very few units on the Bramalea launch -- it's in the range of 40,000 units -- and not a lot of profit associated with it."
He said Chrysler is not making much profit on the LH cars, which include the Dodge Intrepid, Chrysler Concorde and Chrysler LHS, because Chrysler is offering incentives of $1,500 on each of the cars.
He said Chrysler's car lines are generally profitable, but declined to talk about the profitability of specific models.
The minivan launch in 1995 took longer than anticipated, affecting about 25 percent of Chrysler's volume.
